headline: For a sterling investor, Gradient’s assumptions imply a near-full dollar hedge is best
takeaway: Why: Gradient’s dollar and sterling cash rates are almost equal (3.21% and 3.16%), so hedging gives up almost no carry. Meanwhile the dollar is assumed to lose 0.91% a year against an unhedged sterling investor, with 6.75% volatility. Hedging removes both, so the implied ratio keeps rising toward a full hedge.
